events.title: Five charter amendments on the ballot
events.note: Mamdani's Commission on Government Efficiency adopted its final report and five ballot proposals on July 23, after 10 public hearings that drew 1,220 New Yorkers, 264 live testimonies and 603 written submissions. Prop 1 merges the sidewalk and roadway dining approvals into one application, cutting an eight-month process to two. Prop 2 simplifies procurement for small businesses and nonprofits. Prop 3 lets the Department of Transportation fast-track street safety work including bike lanes, and speeds the sale or lease of small city properties. Prop 4 creates one permitting hub for 40 approvals now spread across 18 offices. Prop 5 sets a rainy day fund target of 12% of total tax revenues and requires a deposit formula. After the election the commission becomes a standing advisory board.

events.title: Jackie Robinson breaks baseball's color barrier — 80th anniversary
events.note: Jackie Robinson debuted at first base for the Brooklyn Dodgers, becoming the first Black player in the modern major leagues.

events.title: Studio 54 opens — 50th anniversary

events.title: Lever House brings the glass curtain wall to Park Avenue — 75th anniversary
events.note: Gordon Bunshaft's Lever House, for Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, opened at 390 Park Avenue. Its blue-green glass skin was among the first true curtain walls on an American office tower.

events.title: Local Law 97 annual emissions report due
events.note: Large buildings must file annual emissions reports each May 1. The first were due May 1, 2025, not 2026; penalties run about $268 per metric ton of carbon dioxide equivalent over a building's limit.

events.title: Trinity Church receives its royal charter — 330th anniversary
events.note: The Anglican parish of Trinity Church was chartered on May 6, 1697, on behalf of King William III by Royal Governor Benjamin Fletcher.

events.title: Live TV's Golden Age begins with Kraft Theatre — 80th anniversary
events.note: The premiere of Kraft Television Theatre on May 7, 1947 opened the Golden Age of live television drama, an era of anthology plays broadcast largely from New York studios.

events.title: Lindbergh gets a ticker-tape hero's welcome — 100th anniversary

events.title: Juneteenth
events.note: A public holiday. City offices are closed, no hearings sit and alternate side parking is suspended.

events.title: Rent Guidelines Board final vote
events.note: The rent adjustment for roughly a million rent-stabilized apartments, for leases beginning October 2027. Date estimated from recent practice (June 17, 2024; June 30, 2025; June 25, 2026).

events.title: Fiscal 2028 budget adoption
events.note: The Charter's trigger date is June 5 (section 254), but in practice adoption lands at the end of June: the fiscal 2027 deal was struck and voted on June 30, 2026, hours before the deadline. Date estimated from that practice.

events.title: Slavery ends in New York State — 200th anniversary
events.note: An 1817 law took full effect on July 4, 1827, ending legal slavery in New York and freeing thousands of remaining enslaved people.

events.title: Independence Day observed
events.note: A public holiday. City offices are closed, no hearings sit and alternate side parking is suspended.

events.title: The blackout that broke the city's spirit — 50th anniversary
events.note: Lightning strikes knocked out power for some 25 hours, unleashing widespread looting and arson across the crime-plagued, cash-strapped city.

events.title: Silent Parade marches down Fifth Avenue — 110th anniversary
events.note: Thousands of Black New Yorkers marched in silence down Fifth Avenue to protest lynchings and the East St. Louis massacre.

events.title: The Son of Sam is captured — 50th anniversary
events.note: Police arrested David Berkowitz, ending a serial-killing spree that terrorized the city for more than a year.

events.title: The Plaza Hotel opens facing Central Park — 120th anniversary
events.note: Henry Hardenbergh's Plaza Hotel opened at Fifth Avenue and Central Park South. The French Renaissance chateau-style tower quickly became the grandest hotel in the city.

events.title: Citicorp Center opens, then is secretly reinforced — 50th anniversary
events.note: Hugh Stubbins and engineer William LeMessurier completed Citicorp Center, a 59-story tower on stilts with a distinctive sloped top. A year later a hidden structural flaw prompted a secret emergency repair.

events.title: Joseph Papp's Public Theater opens with "Hair" — 60th anniversary
events.note: Joseph Papp opened his year-round Public Theater in the former Astor Library on Lafayette Street, launching it with the rock musical "Hair," the first production in its new home.

events.title: Prospect Park opens in Brooklyn — 160th anniversary
events.note: The first section of Prospect Park, designed by Olmsted and Vaux, opened to the public in Brooklyn.

events.title: Truck attack on Hudson River bike path — 10th anniversary
events.note: A man drove a rented truck down a Lower Manhattan bike path, killing eight people and injuring many others. It was the city's deadliest terrorist attack since 9/11.

events.title: The African Free School opens — 240th anniversary
events.note: The Manumission Society opened the African Free School, the first school in New York for the children of enslaved and free Black families.

events.title: New York men vote for women's suffrage — 110th anniversary
events.note: New York became the first major eastern state to grant women the vote when male voters approved a suffrage referendum.

events.title: Ed Koch is elected mayor — 50th anniversary
events.note: The brash congressman won the mayoralty, beginning three terms that spanned the city's recovery from fiscal collapse.

events.title: Times Square is reborn — 30th anniversary
events.note: Disney's The Lion King opened at the restored New Amsterdam Theatre, symbolizing the transformation of a once-seedy Times Square into a family tourist mecca.

events.title: Holland Tunnel opens under the Hudson — 100th anniversary
events.note: The Holland Tunnel opened as the first mechanically ventilated underwater vehicular tunnel in the world, linking Manhattan and Jersey City.

events.title: Delmonico's opens — 200th anniversary
events.note: The Swiss-born Delmonico brothers opened a small café on William Street that grew into America's pioneering fine-dining restaurant.
